title: The sunnah as second
hook: the sunnah explains and details the Qur'an

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Qur'an as first source, and your line: the book first. When a question came up, did you go to the source before the opinions? Day one thousand one hundred seventy.

A group of young men have spent some days with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and now they're about to set off home to their people. The Qur'an gives them the command, in Pickthall's words: "Establish worship." It gives it again and again. What it doesn't give is a step-by-step. When to stand, how to bow, what to say, how many units: the text leaves that out. So before they go, in a report kept in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet tells them how to teach the prayer. Pray as you have seen me praying. Today: the sunnah as second.
screen: `ESTABLISH WORSHIP.` → `BUT HOW?` → `PRAY AS YOU HAVE SEEN ME PRAYING.`

segments.voice: First, what sunnah means here. The Prophet's way: what he said, did and approved, carried in the hadith the last block was all about. In fiqh it stands second, right after the Qur'an. Second, the book points to it. The Qur'an says Allah sent the reminder down to the Prophet so that he would explain to people what had been sent down to them. And it tells believers, in Pickthall's words, "Obey Allah, and obey the messenger." The second source isn't bolted on from outside; the first source names it. Third, how it explains. Scholars describe the sunnah doing more than one job. It details what the Qur'an gives in brief, like the prayer: pray as you have seen me praying. It shows how a general command is carried out: the Qur'an commands the poor-due, and the sunnah sets out which wealth is due and how much. It confirms what the Qur'an already says. And scholars discuss, and differ over, rulings found in the sunnah that the Qur'an doesn't mention. Fourth, who carries it. Sunni schools receive the sunnah through the reports of the companions, weighed by the methods of the last block. Shia scholars receive it also through the Imams of the Prophet's family, whose words and example they hold to be part of it, weighed through their own collections. Both put the sunnah right after the book. That's why the hadith block came first: the second source rests on knowing which reports are sound.
screen: `THE PROPHET'S WAY, SECOND.` · `THE BOOK NAMES IT.` · `IT DETAILS, SHOWS AND CONFIRMS.` · `SUNNI AND SHIA CHANNELS.`

segments.voice: The practice: learn one detail from the sunnah. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a prayer you've seen, or prayed: someone standing, then bowing, then resting their forehead on the ground. The Qur'an speaks of bowing and prostrating. The shape of those movements, one after another, comes from people watching the Prophet pray and doing what they saw. Picture the movements slowly, in order. Then come back to your own body: how you're sitting, where your hands are, how you're breathing. Each of those movements was something someone saw, and passed on. The bell holds the time.
The sunnah as second. The Prophet's way, carried in the hadith, standing after the Qur'an in fiqh and explaining it. Today's word.

Your line: the sunnah explains. Today, when an instruction reaches you in brief, look for someone's example of how it's actually done. Tomorrow: consensus of scholars. Day one thousand one hundred seventy.

howItsDone: Muslims learn the details of prayer, charity and fasting from the sunnah, by watching parents and teachers pray and by studying the hadith and the fiqh built on them.
